---
url: /myco/tutorials/first-item.md
---
# Your first item

A guided walk through one task's lifecycle: scaffold a ledger,
create a task, move it through the state machine, and close it —
seeing the markdown change under you each step.

You'll need `myco` installed (see
[getting started](../getting-started.md)) and a git repo to play
in:

```sh
mkdir ledger-demo && cd ledger-demo
git init && git commit --allow-empty -m init
```

## 1. Scaffold the ledger

```sh
myco init
```

This creates a `project/` directory — actually a git worktree of
the new orphan `project` branch — seeded with `TODO.md`,
`BACKLOG.md`, `index.md`, `meta.toml`, and empty item dirs.
`git worktree list` shows it; `.gitignore` hides it from your
code branch.

## 2. Add a task

```sh
myco todo add "write the tutorial" --pri high --label docs
```

```text
added T-001 open pri:high #docs write the tutorial
```

myco allocated `T-001` (the `t` counter in `meta.toml`) and
appended one line to `project/TODO.md`:

```markdown
- [ ] T-001 write the tutorial · pri:high · created:2026-10-29 · #docs
```

Everything after the title is `·`-separated tokens —
`status:`, `pri:`, `owner:`, `created:`, `#label`, `blocks:`,
`links:`, `epic:`, `ms:`, `due:`, `est:`, `cycle:`, `note:` (see
[the file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md) for the full
grammar).

Nest a sub-task under it:

```sh
myco todo add "review it" --parent T-001
```

Children are `- [ ]` lines indented two spaces under the parent.
They are full items — same metadata, same state machine — and
`done`/`defer` on a parent act on the whole subtree.

## 3. Move it through the state machine

```sh
myco item set T-001 --status in-progress --owner devin
myco view board
```

```text
+---------+-----------------+---------+--------------------------+---------+
| Backlog | Open            | Claimed | In Progress              | Blocked |
+---------+-----------------+---------+--------------------------+---------+
|         | T-002 review it |         | T-001 write the tutorial |         |
+---------+-----------------+---------+--------------------------+---------+
```

Statuses are `open → claimed → in-progress → done`, with
`blocked` and `deferred` off the main path — see
[the file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md#state-machine) for
the legal transitions. `item set` walks the machine one step at a
time; an illegal jump errors and tells you the valid targets.

Park something instead of finishing it:

```sh
myco todo defer T-002   # → deferred; the line moves to BACKLOG.md
myco backlog promote T-002   # → open; back to TODO.md
```

## 4. Leave a handoff

```sh
myco handoff T-001 --note "Done: draft. Next: screenshots." --actor devin
myco resume T-001
```

`handoff` appends a dated entry to `handoffs/T-001.md`;
`resume` prints the minimal restart context — the item, its
`blocks:` deps, latest handoffs, open checklist.

## 5. Finish and check

```sh
myco todo done T-001
myco check
```

```text
check: clean
```

Done tasks move to `DONE.md` — the done archive keeps completed
work browsable (`myco done list`, `myco item show`) instead of
vanishing; the `project` branch history is still the record.
Every verb you ran was one atomic commit
on that branch (`git -C project log --oneline` shows them all).

## Recap

| you ran                          | myco did                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `todo add`                       | alloc id, append line to `TODO.md`          |
| `item set --status`              | one legal state-machine step                |
| `todo defer` / `backlog promote` | move the line TODO ↔ BACKLOG                |
| `handoff` / `resume`             | append-only session notes / restart context |
| `todo done`                      | `done`, line moves to `DONE.md`        |
| `check`                          | validate files, state machine, index drift  |

Every write went through a verb — hand-editing works too (the
markdown is canonical), but `myco check` is the referee either
way.

Next: [the daily agent loop](../how-to/agent-loop.md) for how an
agent drives these verbs, or the
[CLI reference](../reference/cli.md) for the full surface.

url: /myco/how-to/init-repo.md

# Set up myco on a repository

`myco init` turns any git repo into a myco project: an orphan
`project` branch checked out as a `project/` worktree.

```sh
cd your-repo
myco init
```

## What it creates

| path                                                            | what                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `project/`                                                      | git worktree on the orphan `project` branch                    |
| `project/meta.toml`                                             | repo name + per-kind id counters (`[next]`)                    |
| `project/TODO.md`                                               | active tasks                                                   |
| `project/BACKLOG.md`                                            | deferred items                                                 |
| `project/DONE.md`                                               | done archive — completed tasks stay browsable                  |
| `project/index.md`                                              | human-readable ledger index                                    |
| `project/issues/`, `proposals/`, `plans/`, `adrs/`, `handoffs/` | file-backed item dirs                                          |
| `myco.toml`                                                      | repo-root config — seeded with the commented `[[kinds]]` prelude (only when absent) |
| `.gitignore` += `project/`                                      | keeps the worktree out of code commits                         |
| `AGENTS.md`                                                     | gains a marker-delimited, myco-managed *Agent awareness* block |

`init` commits the scaffold on the `project` branch — your code
branch gains `myco.toml` (the commented kinds prelude, only when
the file doesn't already exist), the `.gitignore` line, and the
`AGENTS.md` block. The block teaches agents the myco workflow; it's delimited
by `<!-- myco:agent-awareness -->` markers so prose elsewhere in
the file is preserved — a hand-written *Agent awareness* section
is upgraded in place. `check` validates it as an
`agents-md` finding and `check --fix` repairs it.

## Re-running init

`init` is idempotent: a valid existing worktree gets its scaffold
verified/repaired instead of re-created. It is the safe "is this
repo set up?" probe. `myco org init` re-runs it on every
registered repo — the rollout path when scaffolding (like the
`AGENTS.md` block) is introduced or updated. Repos registered
`ledger = "none"` (intentionally ledger-less org members) are
skipped — see [org views](org-views.md#ledger-less-repos--one-org-wide-ledger).

## Overrides and discovery

`--root` picks the repo, `--dir` picks a non-default worktree
path (init uses it instead of `<root>/project`):

```sh
myco init --root ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia
myco init --dir ~/work/ledger          # worktree somewhere else
```

Every other verb discovers the project the same way, in order:

1. `--dir` — explicit worktree path (must qualify as a myco project)
2. `--root` — repo root (worktree is `<root>/project`)
3. cwd inside the project worktree itself
4. `project_dir` in `myco.toml` (see [config](../reference/config.md))
5. walk up from cwd for a `project/` worktree on branch `project`
6. org-ledger fallback — a *registered* repo with no ledger of its
   own resolves to the org ledger (see
   [org views](org-views.md#ledger-less-repos--one-org-wide-ledger))

A non-standard worktree location stays discoverable if you set
`project_dir` (relative to the repo root) in a `myco.toml` —
the search order is `$MYCO_CONFIG` → `./myco.toml` (where you
run `myco`) → `~/.config/myco/myco.toml`.

## If the repo has a `pm/` dir

Don't `init` — run [`myco migrate`](migrate.md) instead. It
converts the legacy `pm/` layout into a fresh `project/` worktree
in one pass.

# Run the daily agent loop

The core loop for an agent (or a human driving like one):
orient → claim → work → hand off → resume. Every step is a verb;
`--json` on all of them.

## Orient

```sh
myco status --prompt    # token-sized digest, sized for a context window
```

`status --prompt` is the session opener: counts by kind, what's
in progress, what's open — enough to pick work without reading
the files. `myco status` (no flag) is the human-readable version;
`myco view board` and `myco report` give the kanban and the trend.
Boards cap at a screenful of rows — `--all` shows every card.
For a human at the wheel, `myco ui` is the same board as a
full-screen TUI — see
[the interactive board](../getting-started.md#the-interactive-board).

## Claim

```sh
myco item set T-012 --status claimed --owner devin
myco item set T-012 --status in-progress
```

`claimed` says "an actor owns this" before work starts;
`in-progress` says "being worked now". Both are single legal
steps from `open`. Owner ids are namespaced actor strings —
`devin`, `human:luis`, … — so multiple agents can share a ledger.

Hit a wall mid-task: `myco item set T-012 --status blocked`.
Need the details: `myco item show T-012` (add `--json` for the
full item + location + body).

Fan-out reads (a resume + two shows + a view) batch into one
call — `myco batch` maps NDJSON requests onto the whole `myco
serve` surface, one JSON-RPC response per line:

```sh
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"id":1,"method":"resume","params":{"id":"T-012"}}' \
  '{"id":2,"method":"view","params":{"name":"open"}}' \
  | myco batch
```

## Hand off

Before the session ends, leave resumable state on the item:

```sh
myco handoff T-012 --actor devin --session cli:$$ \
  --note "Done: parser landed. Next: emitter. Open: archive semantics."
```

`--note -` reads stdin — pipe a generated summary. See
[handoffs](handoff.md) for the full verb behavior.

## Resume

Next session — human or agent — pulls the restart context:

```sh
myco resume T-012          # compact prompt-ready block
myco resume T-012 --json   # {item, location, blocks_titles, links_titles, handoffs, handoffs_total, open_checklist}
```

Then `myco status --prompt` for the ledger-wide picture and the
loop restarts.

## Hygiene

```sh
myco check          # exits 1 on error-severity findings (--fix repairs what it safely can)
myco check --fix    # safe repairs + one commit
```

Run `check` when files were hand-edited or the index may have
drifted — it validates the [file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md),
state machine, and index snapshots.

## No-commit mode

Batch or scripted flows can skip the per-verb commit with
`--no-commit` or `MYCO_NO_COMMIT=1`, then commit once:

```sh
myco commit -m "chore: end-of-day ledger tidy"
```

`myco commit` stages all worktree changes and commits with a
conventional message (default `chore: update project ledger`).

---

---
url: /myco/how-to/handoff.md
---
# Hand off work between sessions

Attach resumable state to any item at the end of a working
session, then pull the minimal context to restart it later.

```sh
myco handoff T-012 --note "parser done, emitter next" --actor devin --session cli:abc123
myco resume T-012   # minimal context block to restart work
```

## `myco handoff <id>`

Appends a dated entry to `handoffs/<ID>.md` — works on every item
kind (`T-`, `I-`, `P-`, `ADR-`, `PL-`), live or archived. The item
must exist; the note is required.

* `--note "…"` — the handoff text (done/next/open). `-` reads stdin.
* `--actor <id>` — who wrote it (`devin`, `human:luis`; default `cli`).
* `--session <id>` — provenance, any id string (a sepia session id,
  `cli:<pid>`, …). Recorded verbatim, never interpreted.

Each call is one appended `##` entry and one commit
(`chore: handoff <id>`). Files are append-only — history inside a
file is never rewritten.

## `myco resume <id> [--last N]`

Emits the restart context as a compact prompt block:

```text
I-003 in-progress pri:high owner:devin #index memory leak
in: issues/issue-0003-memory-leak.md
blocks:
  T-010 store layer
handoffs:
2026-10-29 · devin · session:cli:abc123
  Done: repro. Next: fix.
open checklist:
  - [ ] add regression test
```

`--json` gives `{item, location, blocks_titles, links_titles,
handoffs[], handoffs_total, open_checklist}` — the same data for
machines. `--last N` shows
only the latest N handoff entries (default 10).

`myco item show <id>` surfaces a `handoffs: N` count; `myco check`
keeps `handoffs/` honest — files for removed items are archived to
`handoffs/archive/` by `--fix`, and malformed entries are parse
findings.

For the sepia-side wiring (session hooks calling these verbs), see
[session continuity with sepia](session-continuity.md).

---

---
url: /myco/how-to/session-continuity.md
---
# Session continuity with sepia

sepia owns session lifecycle; myco owns work memory. The boundary
is two verbs — no sepia code lives in this repo, and no myco code
in sepia. Each side just calls the other's CLI.

## The pattern

Session end (sepia hook) — leave a resumable note on the item you
were working, tagged with the sepia session id:

```sh
myco handoff T-012 \
  --actor devin \
  --session <sepia-session-id> \
  --note "Done: store layer landed. Next: wire verbs. Open: archive semantics for ADRs."
```

`--note -` reads stdin, so a hook can pipe a generated summary.
`--session` accepts any id string — a sepia session id, a
`cli:<pid>:<ts>` fallback, whatever wrote the entry. It's
provenance only; myco records it and never interprets it.

Session start — pull the minimal restart context into the prompt:

```sh
myco resume T-012 --json
```

`resume` returns the item (status, priority, owner, labels), the
titles of its `blocks:` dependencies and `links:` associations,
the latest handoff entries (`handoffs` + `handoffs_total`), and
the unchecked `- [ ]` checklist items for file-backed items —
the single-item counterpart of `myco status --prompt`. Human
output is a compact prompt-ready block; `--last N` caps the
entries shown (default 10).

## Abnormal endings — `myco interrupt`

A session that dies mid-work shouldn't leave items claimed
forever. `myco interrupt` is the teardown verb:

```sh
myco interrupt T-012 --note "session crashed" --actor devin
myco interrupt --session cli:abc123        # every item claimed under it
```

With an id, the item walks a legal step back to `open` (from
`in-progress`/`blocked`/`claimed`) and gains an `interrupted`
handoff entry in the same commit — `myco item show` and the board
flag it with `⚡` until real work resumes. Without an id,
`--session <id>` reverts every item whose claim was tagged with
that session (claims made via `item set --session`/`--claim`).

## Where handoffs live

`handoffs/<ID>.md` — one append-only file per item, uniform across
every kind:

```markdown
+++
item = "T-012"
+++

# Handoffs — T-012

## 2026-10-29 · devin · session:cli:abc123

Done: store layer landed. Next: wire verbs. Open: archive semantics for ADRs.
```

Entries are never rewritten — each `myco handoff` is one appended
`## <date> · <actor> · session:<id>` heading and one atomic commit
(`chore: handoff T-012`) on the `project` branch, so the branch
history is the audit trail.

When an item is done it doesn't disappear — the whole subtree
moves to `DONE.md`, the done archive. `myco done list` browses it
with the same filters as the other lists, and `myco item show`
still resolves it, so its handoff file stays live. A handoff only
becomes orphaned when the item is truly gone; `myco check`
reports it and `myco check --fix` moves it to
`handoffs/archive/`: the live dir stays clean, the knowledge
survives, and `myco resume` on an archived item still finds it.

# Migrate a legacy ledger

`myco migrate` brings pre-v2 ledgers up to the current spec.
Two modes, auto-detected by what's on disk.

## `pm/` → `project/`

A `pm/` directory at the repo root is the pre-worktree layout.
One command converts and removes it:

```sh
cd your-repo
myco migrate
```

* `pm/TODO.md` / `pm/BACKLOG.md` bullets become `T-` items in the
  new `TODO.md` / `BACKLOG.md` — done items are dropped
* `pm/ROADMAP.md` becomes a `plans/` file
* any other `pm/*.md` becomes an `issues/` file
* a fresh `project/` worktree is scaffolded (the `init` path)
* `pm/` is removed and its deletion committed on the code branch

## Legacy `project/` → v2

Files already on a `project` branch are normalized in place:

* id-less items get ids
* `[x]`/done items drop (history keeps them)
* heading-like lines become `##` sections
* frontmatter-less files in item dirs are *adopted* — the
  filename's number is honored when free (`0001-foo.md` →
  `ADR-0001`); collisions take the next unclaimed number with a
  warning. Adopted files get synthesized frontmatter and the
  canonical name
* everything is re-emitted canonically

## After migrating

```sh
myco check        # should report clean
myco status       # the ledger, v2-shaped
```

`--json` on `migrate` returns the run's counters — items
converted, ids allocated, files moved, warnings. If the run left
unparsed lines, they're listed there; fix by hand and `check`
again.

url: /myco/how-to/import-work.md
---
# Import external work

`myco absorb` pulls work that lives elsewhere into the ledger —
code comments, Jira exports, GitHub issue dumps.

## Sweep code comments

```sh
myco absorb comments                  # the repo root
myco absorb comments --path src/ --kinds TODO,FIXME,HACK
myco absorb comments --to issues      # file issues instead of backlog items
myco absorb comments --dry            # report without creating
```

Uses ripgrep (`rg` must be installed), respects `.gitignore`, and
skips `project/`, `docs/`, `target/`. Findings land as `T-` items
— `BACKLOG.md` by default, `issues/` files with `--to issues`.

## Jira CSV

```sh
myco absorb jira export.csv
myco absorb jira export.csv --include-done
```

`Done`/`Resolved` rows are skipped unless `--include-done` — then
they're created `done` and archived.

## GitHub issue dump

```sh
myco absorb github dump.json          # or dump.csv
myco absorb github dump.json --include-done
```

JSON input is an array of issue objects — a
`gh issue list --json number,title,state,labels,assignees,body`
dump works as-is (`labels` entries can be `"name"` strings or
`{name:…}` objects, `assignee`/`assignees` strings or
`{login:…}` objects; extra fields are ignored). CSV is the
equivalent columns. `closed` issues are skipped unless
`--include-done` (created `done` + archived).

## After importing

```sh
myco status         # the ledger, now bigger
myco view board     # or the kanban view
myco check          # sanity
```

Each absorb run is one commit — `--no-commit` batches several
imports into one `myco commit`.

url: /myco/how-to/views.md
---
# Shape the board with named views

A view is a declarative spec — `filter`, `group_by`, `sort`,
`limit`, `format` — evaluated by one engine. Names come from two
places: built-in presets (`board`, `open`, `epic`, `milestone`,
`next`, `org-board`, `org-status`) and `[views.<name>]` tables in
`myco.toml` ([spec fields](../reference/config.md)).

## Define one

```toml
# myco.toml
[views.hot]
filter = { pri_min = "high", status = ["open", "in-progress"] }
group_by = "owner"
sort = "-created"
format = "list"
```

```sh
myco view hot          # resolves the named view
myco view              # lists every defined view + origin — or renders
                       # `default_view` from config when one is set
myco view --status open --pri-min high   # ad-hoc spec from flags
myco view hot --limit 3                  # flags patch the named spec
```

Every read is also `--json`: `{view, spec, groups, interrupted}`.

## Views are the read surface

`myco view <name>` is *the* lens — there are no per-view verbs.
`view board` renders the kanban (Backlog | Open | Claimed | In
Progress | Blocked lanes); `view epic` and `view milestone` group
by that metadata, one column per group with `ungrouped` trailing.
`view next` is the "what do I pick up" preset — one open task or
issue, top of the default sort. `view org-board`/`org-status` are
the index-sourced org presets (see
[org views](org-views.md)).
The filter flags scope any view — `myco view board --epic v2` is
one epic's lanes.

A config view shadowing a built-in name redefines `myco view <name>`
itself:

```toml
[views.board]
filter = { kind = ["issue"] } # view board is now issues-only
```

A shadow warns on stderr (`view "board" shadows the built-in
preset`) and `myco check` lints the repo layer's specs. The lane
chrome applies only to a status-grouped board spec: a shadowed
spec with a non-status `group_by` renders generic columns headed
by the group labels, and `--json` emits the `{view, spec, groups,
interrupted}` payload instead of the five-lane map. Specs that
admit non-lane buckets (e.g. `done`) surface them as extra
columns/keys — nothing matched is silently dropped.

Layering is repo < user < flags: a `[views]` table merges
across config layers; scalar fields stay first-match.

## Over the wire

`myco serve` exposes `view` (`{name?, spec?}` — `spec` is the
same per-field patch) alongside the rest of the verb surface;
`myco batch` reaches all of it one-shot:

```sh
printf '{"id":1,"method":"view","params":{"name":"hot"}}\n' | myco batch
```

## Verbs on top of views — `[verbs]`

`[verbs.<name>]` declares a verb of your own (P-007): `myco <name>`
then works like a builtin on every front end — CLI,
`myco batch`, and `myco serve` (it joins `initialize`'s method
list). Two kinds, both read-only:

```toml
# view-emit — a ViewSpec baked to one emit shape
[verbs.hot]
emit = "first"                     # table | json | ids | first
filter = { pri_min = "high", status = ["open"] }
sort = ["pri", "id"]

# alias — argv baked for a read-only builtin
[verbs.standup]
target = "view"
args = ["open"]
```

`myco hot` prints the top open high-priority item (`first` is
`next`-shaped but can't claim); `myco standup` is `myco view
open` with extra tokens appended (`myco standup --limit 3`).
`ids` prints one id per line — pipeable. `--json` works on every
kind.

Load-time rules: a verb name colliding with a builtin warns and
the builtin wins; an alias to a mutating or missing target warns
and is skipped; a view-emit spec goes through the same
`ViewSpec` validation as `[views]` — `myco check` lints the repo
layer's `[verbs]` (`verb-invalid` findings). Repo verbs merge
over user verbs on the same name (repo is shared surface);
verbs are named with the bare-word space only — a config verb
can't shadow inside a group.

Composites and hiding builtins are deferred — see
`proposal-0007`.

---

---
url: /myco/how-to/org-views.md
---
# See work across repos

`myco index` registers repos into a machine-wide cache;
index-sourced `myco view` specs render cross-repo views over it.
The org is just a view over the index universe — every filter,
grouping, and format the view engine has applies to it.

## The index

The index lives under `$MYCO_HOME`, else `$XDG_DATA_HOME/myco`,
else `~/.local/share/myco`:

* `repos.toml` — the registry (`[[repo]] path name`), a plain
  file you can inspect
* `index.redb` — one `snapshots` table: repo path → JSON snapshot

It is a **derived, disposable cache** — markdown in each repo's
`project/` stays canonical. `rm -rf` the index dir and
`myco index rebuild` derives it back.

## Register repos

```sh
myco index add ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia    # repo root or its project/ worktree
myco index add .                      # register the repo you're in
myco index list                       # repos + snapshot freshness
```

`add` takes an initial snapshot. Snapshots go stale as ledgers
change — `list` marks them `stale`; index-sourced views
auto-rebuild stale entries on read, or rebuild explicitly:

```sh
myco index rebuild                    # all registered repos
myco index rebuild ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia
myco index remove ~/GitHub/9aia/sepia # unregister + drop snapshot
```

## Ledger-less repos — one org-wide ledger

The registry distinguishes three ledger states per repo, via the
`ledger` key in `repos.toml` (absent = `local`, the conventional
reading):

* `local` — the repo's own `project/` worktree (the `worktree`
  key, else `<path>/project`).
* `none` — explicitly ledger-less: an org member with no
  `project/` at all.
* `org` — the org/global ledger: the *one* repo whose worktree
  every ledger-less member resolves to.

`myco index add` observes the state: a git repo with no
qualifying worktree registers as `none` and takes no snapshot;
`--org` marks the global ledger (and clears the mark on any
other entry — at most one).

```sh
myco index add ~/GitHub/9aia/project --org   # the one global ledger
myco index add ~/GitHub/handl-lang/engine    # ledger-less → "none"
```

Inside a registered `none` repo, verbs that need a project —
`status`, `todo add`, `view`, writes included — resolve to the
org ledger's worktree instead of failing. Unregistered repos
still fail as before; `--dir`, `--root`, `MYCO_CONFIG`, and
`project_dir` keep top precedence. `none` entries are omitted
from index-sourced org views (no rows, no warnings), report
`no-ledger` under `index rebuild`/`index list`, and are skipped
by `org init` — the rollout never scaffolds `project/` into
them. `ledger` is a plain hand-editable `repos.toml` key.

## Org views — `view --source index`

Two built-in presets run on the index universe:

```sh
myco view org-status                  # per-repo grouped list
myco view org-board                   # org kanban — repo-prefixed cards
myco view org-board --all             # every card — no row cap
myco view org-board --md              # markdown table for docs/READMEs
```

`org-status` is one `label (n)` bucket per registered repo — the
old `org status` digest's substitute. `org-board` merges every
repo's live items into the five lanes; cards are prefixed with
the repo name (`thal:T-118 …`) so one board spans the whole org.

Under the hood both are plain view specs with `source = "index"`
— the same thing works ad-hoc or in your own `[views]` config:

```sh
myco view --source index --group-by status --format board   # org-board minus its live-status filter
myco view --source index --group-by owner                   # who has what, org-wide
myco view org-board --kind issue --label bug                # filters still apply
myco view org-status --status open,claimed                  # active items only
```

```toml
# ~/.config/myco/myco.toml — a personal org preset
[views.hot-org]
source = "index"
filter = { pri_min = "high" }
group_by = "repo"
```

Items in an index-sourced view carry their repo tag: `group_by = "repo"` buckets by it, cards and list lines prefix `repo:ID`,
and `--json` items gain a `"repo"` field. Snapshots hold no
handoff state, so the `⚡` interrupted marker (and the
`"interrupted"` JSON flag) is repo-source only. A repo whose
worktree vanished keeps contributing its last snapshot and the
read warns on stderr.

## Board output

Human boards — `view`'s board format (`view board`, `view epic`,
`view org-board`, …) — are fitted to the terminal: sized to its
width (`$MYCO_WIDTH` overrides; 100 columns when piped) and
capped at a screenful of rows (~25) with a `… +N more` footer —
`--all` lifts the cap. `--md` and `--json` are unbounded. Output
is ANSI-colored on a tty: `NO_COLOR` disables color,
`CLICOLOR_FORCE`/`FORCE_COLOR` force it on.

On a tty the long views — boards, `index list` — page through
`$MYCO_PAGER`, else `$PAGER`, else `less -FRSX` (the `-F` means a
single screenful still exits instantly). An empty
`MYCO_PAGER`/`PAGER` disables paging; piped output always prints
directly.

For a fully interactive board — TODO/BACKLOG tabs, item preview,
done/defer/promote by key, including index-sourced `org-*` views
(`myco ui --view org-board`) — see
[`myco ui`](../getting-started.md#the-interactive-board).

---

---
url: /myco/how-to/custom-kinds.md
---
# Declare custom item kinds

`[[kinds]]` tables in `myco.toml` extend the five prelude kinds
(task, issue, proposal, adr, plan) with your own — a `spike`
folder of experiment write-ups, a `decision` log, whatever the
ledger needs. `myco init` seeds the whole prelude as comments in
the repo-root `myco.toml`; uncomment a block to restate a builtin,
or append entries to declare new kinds.

## Declare one

```toml
# myco.toml (repo root — or ~/.config/myco/myco.toml for all repos)

[[kinds]]
name      = "spike"
prefix    = "S"               # [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*, ≤ 15 bytes — S-001 is now a real id
storage   = "dir"             # dir = one file per item; doc = ledger lines
dir       = "spikes"          # optional — defaults to <name>s
done_state = "done"           # the status that resolves the item
zero_pad  = 3                 # S-001 vs ADR-0001
```

Field reference (all but `name`/`prefix`/`storage` optional —
full list in [config](../reference/config.md)):

| field          | meaning                                                        |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`         | vocabulary name — `kind = ["spike"]` in views, `S-` ids        |
| `prefix`       | id prefix — must not collide with another kind's prefix        |
| `storage`      | `doc` (ledger lines) or `dir` (one md file per item)           |
| `dir`          | `dir` storage subdirectory — defaults to `<name>s`             |
| `file_prefix`  | filename prefix — defaults to `name`; `""` gives `0004-slug.md` |
| `states`       | the statuses this kind may carry — defaults to the full machine |
| `done_state`   | the resolving status — `done` unless declared otherwise        |
| `supersede`    | `superseded_by:`/`supersedes:` frontmatter is meaningful       |
| `resolve_verb` | declaration only in v1 — no verb reads it yet                  |
| `zero_pad`     | digits in emitted ids — 3 default                              |

## What you get for free

A declared kind rides the generic surface — no new verbs:

* **files** — `dir` kinds get `spikes/spike-NNNN-<slug>.md` with
  the same `+++` frontmatter + markdown body as issues and
  plans ([file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md)); `doc` kinds
  live in the ledger docs
* **verbs** — `myco item show S-001`, `item set` (status walks
  *this kind's* `states`), `item move`, `handoff`, `resume`,
  `interrupt` all work on any declared id
* **views** — `kind = ["spike"]` (or `["S"]`) filters any view;
  `group_by = "kind"` buckets mixed ledgers
* **checks** — `myco check` validates the kind's files, ids, and
  state machine, and lints the `[[kinds]]` table itself
  (`kind-invalid` findings)

## Restating a prelude kind

Naming a `[[kinds]]` entry `issue` *shadows* the builtin spec —
restating it verbatim is a no-op (that's what the commented seed
shows), and changing fields like `states` or `done_state`
reconfigures the kind. The `prefix` is locked: `issue`'s `I` is
identity — reinterpreting it would rewrite every existing id, so
a mismatched prefix is a config error. Repo `myco.toml` wins a
name collision over `~/.config/myco/myco.toml` — a repo's kind
vocabulary is shared surface.

## Creating items

There are no per-kind `new` verbs for custom kinds (the prelude
kinds keep theirs — `issue new`, `plan new`, …). Author the item
file per the [file spec](../explanation/file-spec.md) —
`spikes/spike-0001-<slug>.md` with `id = "S-001"` frontmatter —
then `myco check` validates it and the verbs take over from
there. Keep the `[next]` counters in `project/meta.toml` ahead of
the ids you hand out, or the next `alloc` collides.

## `myco`

myco — agent-first project management for a repo's `project/` worktree.

**Usage:** `myco [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `todo` — TODO.md tasks — add / done / defer / list.
* `backlog` — BACKLOG.md parked items — add / promote / list.
* `done` — DONE.md — the done-task archive `todo done` lands in.
* `issue` — Tracked issues, one file each under `issues/`.
* `proposal` — Design proposals under `proposals/` (`P-NNN`).
* `plan` — Execution plans under `plans/` (`PL-NNN`).
* `adr` — Architecture decision records under `adrs/` (`ADR-NNNN`).
* `item` — Kind-agnostic item verbs — show / set / move.
* `absorb` — Import work into the ledger — TODO/FIXME comments, Jira CSV exports, GitHub issue dumps.
* `index` — The derived index: register repos, query/rebuild snapshots.
* `org` — Cross-repo scaffolding — re-run `init` on every registered repo. Cross-repo *views* are `myco view org-board|org-status` (index-sourced).
* `manifest` — Capabilities + protocol version — agent self-discovery.
* `schema` — The file/state spec, machine-readable JSON Schema.
* `init` — Scaffold `project/`: orphan branch + worktree + .gitignore + seed files + the managed AGENTS.md agent-awareness block. Idempotent — existing worktree and AGENTS.md prose are preserved, only the marked block is (re)written.
* `check` — Validate the ledger (schemas, state machine, ids, refs) and the worktree it lives in (detached HEAD, wrong branch, unpushed commits); also validates the managed AGENTS.md block on the repo root. Findings carry a severity: `error` exits 1, `warning` is reported and costs nothing (ADR-0002). `--fix` applies safe repairs + commits, including reattaching a detached worktree.
* `migrate` — Convert legacy ledgers to v2: `pm/` → `project/`, or normalize files already on the `project` branch.
* `commit` — Stage + commit worktree changes (conventional message).
* `undo` — Undo the last ledger commit — resets the `project` branch tip one back (`HEAD~1`). One verb = one commit, so the reset is the inverse mutation, file deletions included; the undone commit is journaled for `redo`. Refuses on a dirty worktree (uncommitted `--no-commit` writes), at the root commit, and when the tip is already published on `origin` (unless `--force`). `--list` shows the redoable stack without mutating.
* `redo` — Redo the last undo — pops the undo journal and restores the commit `myco undo` moved away from (`git reset --hard <target>`). Repeatable while entries remain; the stack self-invalidates when the ledger moves (any commit/pull/manual git op since the undo). Refuses on a dirty worktree.
* `sync` — Reconcile the ledger branch with `origin/<branch>` — fetch, fast-forward or rebase local commits onto the remote tip, then heal merge damage: `meta.toml` counters reconcile, duplicate ids renumber remote-wins (the pushed item keeps its id; the local one moves, refs stay bound to the remote). Mutating verbs refuse while behind (`ensure_synced`), so this is the gate. A rebase conflict stops mid-flight — resolve + `git rebase --continue` + `myco sync` again, or `--abort` to bail.
* `view` — Declarative views — named presets (`[views.<name>]` in config + built-ins `board|open|epic|milestone|next`, plus index-sourced `org-board|org-status` for cross-repo) or an ad-hoc spec from flags (`--source index` unions the registered repos' snapshots). `myco view board` is the kanban; `format = "repos"` emits one row per repo; bare `myco view` lists views (or renders `default_view` when config names one).
* `next` — The single highest-priority open item — "what should I work on" (a `view` eval with limit 1: open tasks+issues, `pri,id`; the filter flags merge over that default). `--claim` mutates it to `claimed` + an owner in one commit.
* `status` — Cheap digest of the work ledger. `--prompt` = token-sized.
* `report` — Aging + velocity + blocked — how the ledger is trending.
* `handoff` — Attach resumable state at session end — appends a dated entry to `handoffs/<ID>.md` (any item kind, live or archived; append-only).
* `interrupt` — A session ended with work still claimed/in-progress/blocked — revert the item to `open` + `interrupted` handoff, one commit. Without an id, `--session <id>` is the teardown: every item claimed under that session reverts in one commit. Session-lifecycle hooks (sepia, CLI session-end) call this; myco never detects sessions itself.
* `resume` — Minimal context block to restart work on an item — the item, `blocks:` dep titles, latest handoffs, open checklist. The single-item `status --prompt`. 1..n ids batch in one call.
* `ui` — Interactive board TUI (ratatui) — TODO/BACKLOG tabs, item preview, writes through the same ops the verbs use; auto-reloads when the ledger changes on disk. `--view` with a `source = "index"` spec (org-\*) opens the cross-repo index board: `repo:ID` rows, verbs write the owning repo.
* `serve` — Sequential request/response verb surface on stdio — JSON-RPC 2.0, one line in / one line out. For embedding (peregrin spawns one per repo); stdin IS the wire, so no served method reads content from it.
* `batch` — One-shot `serve` — NDJSON verb requests from stdin or `--file`, one JSON-RPC response line per request, dispatched through the same served surface. Per-line errors never fail the run; mutations keep per-request commits (`--no-commit`/`$MYCO_NO_COMMIT` apply). stdin IS the wire here too — requests that would read it are rejected.

###### **Options:**

* `--json` — Emit JSON (accepted everywhere; default output for machines).
* `--no-commit` — Skip the per-verb commit (also suppressed by $MYCO_NO_COMMIT).
* `--dir <PATH>` — Project worktree to act on, overriding discovery.
* `--root <PATH>` — Repo root to act on, overriding discovery (the worktree is `<root>/project`).

## `myco todo`

TODO.md tasks — add / done / defer / list.

**Usage:** `myco todo <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `add` — Add a task — allocs a T-id, appends to a section of TODO.md.
* `done` — Mark done — walks the state machine to `done`, removes the line, and archives the subtree into DONE.md. Done on a parent archives the whole subtree — children die with it. Confirms on a tty (`--yes`/`$MYCO_YES` skips; scripts never prompt).
* `defer` — Park a task — transition to `deferred`, move the line to BACKLOG.md. Defer on a parent moves the whole subtree (children park with it); on a child it detaches alone.
* `list` — List tasks.

## `myco todo add`

Add a task — allocs a T-id, appends to a section of TODO.md.

**Usage:** `myco todo add [OPTIONS] <title>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<TITLE>` — One-line title.

###### **Options:**

* `--section <SECTION>` — Section to add under (created when absent; default: the first section, or an unsectioned run).
* `--parent <PARENT>` — Nest under this task instead of a section — the new item becomes a child (`  - [ ]` under the parent).
* `--pri <PRI>` \[alias: `priority`] — Priority: low|med|high|crit.
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor id (`devin`, `human:luis`, …).
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#label` — repeatable.
* `--blocks <BLOCKS>` — Ids this item blocks — comma-separated or repeatable.
* `--links <LINKS>` — Ids this item is associated with (its plan, proposal, …) — comma-separated or repeatable.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Epic name — the delivery grouping this item belongs to (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Milestone name — the target this item ships under (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).
* `--due <DUE>` — Due date — `YYYY-MM-DD`.
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Estimate in points (0–1000) — relative size, not hours.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Cycle name — the iteration this item is scheduled in (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).

## `myco todo done`

Mark done — walks the state machine to `done`, removes the line, and archives the subtree into DONE.md. Done on a parent archives the whole subtree — children die with it. Confirms on a tty (`--yes`/`$MYCO_YES` skips; scripts never prompt).

**Usage:** `myco todo done [OPTIONS] <id>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Task id (`T-NNN`).

###### **Options:**

* `--yes` — Skip the confirmation prompt (also `$MYCO_YES`; non-interactive runs never prompt).

## `myco todo defer`

Park a task — transition to `deferred`, move the line to BACKLOG.md. Defer on a parent moves the whole subtree (children park with it); on a child it detaches alone.

**Usage:** `myco todo defer <id>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Task id (`T-NNN`).

## `myco todo list`

List tasks.

**Usage:** `myco todo list [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--status <STATUS>` — Keep only items with this status.
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Keep only items owned by this actor.
* `--label <LABEL>` — Keep only items carrying all of these labels (repeatable).
* `--pri <PRI>` — Keep only items at this priority.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Keep only items in this epic.
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Keep only items in this milestone.
* `--due <DUE>` — Keep only items due on this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Keep only items with this point estimate.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Keep only items in this cycle.
* `--query <QUERY>` — Keep only items whose id, title, or a label contains this text (case-insensitive).
* `--limit <N>` — Keep only the first N items after filtering.

## `myco issue`

Tracked issues, one file each under `issues/`.

**Usage:** `myco issue <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `new` — File an issue — allocs an I-id, writes `issues/issue-NNNN-<slug>.md` with frontmatter + template.
* `list` — List issues (live files; `--archived` includes `issues/archive/`).
* `resolve` — Close an issue — walks the state machine to `done`; `--resolution` appends text under `## Resolution`.
* `archive` — Shelve a done issue — moves the file to `issues/archive/`.
* `comment` — Append a dated note under `## Comments` (created when missing).

## `myco issue new`

File an issue — allocs an I-id, writes `issues/issue-NNNN-<slug>.md` with frontmatter + template.

**Usage:** `myco issue new [OPTIONS] <title>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<TITLE>` — One-line title (drives the filename slug).

###### **Options:**

* `--body <FILE|->` — Body markdown from a file, or `-` for stdin.
* `--text <TEXT>` — Body markdown inline.
* `--pri <PRI>` \[alias: `priority`] — Priority: low|med|high|crit.
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor id (`devin`, `human:luis`, …).
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#label` — repeatable.
* `--blocks <BLOCKS>` — Ids this item blocks — comma-separated or repeatable.
* `--links <LINKS>` — Ids this item is associated with (its plan, proposal, …) — comma-separated or repeatable.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Epic name — the delivery grouping this item belongs to (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Milestone name — the target this item ships under (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).
* `--due <DUE>` — Due date — `YYYY-MM-DD`.
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Estimate in points (0–1000) — relative size, not hours.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Cycle name — the iteration this item is scheduled in (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).

## `myco issue list`

List issues (live files; `--archived` includes `issues/archive/`).

**Usage:** `myco issue list [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--archived` — Include archived items.
* `--status <STATUS>` — Keep only items with this status.
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Keep only items owned by this actor.
* `--label <LABEL>` — Keep only items carrying all of these labels (repeatable).
* `--pri <PRI>` — Keep only items at this priority.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Keep only items in this epic.
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Keep only items in this milestone.
* `--due <DUE>` — Keep only items due on this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Keep only items with this point estimate.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Keep only items in this cycle.
* `--query <QUERY>` — Keep only items whose id, title, or a label contains this text (case-insensitive).
* `--limit <N>` — Keep only the first N items after filtering.

## `myco issue resolve`

Close an issue — walks the state machine to `done`; `--resolution` appends text under `## Resolution`.

**Usage:** `myco issue resolve [OPTIONS] <id>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Issue id (`I-NNN`).

###### **Options:**

* `--resolution <RESOLUTION>` — Resolution text appended to the body.

###### **Arguments:**

* `status` — Set a proposal's status. Proposal words alias the state machine: `draft` = open, `accepted` = done, `rejected` = deferred — the transition is walked through the machine, so `accepted` passes `open → in-progress → done`.

* `--pri <PRI>` \[alias: `priority`] — Priority: low|med|high|crit.
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor id (`devin`, `human:luis`, …).
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#label` — repeatable.
* `--blocks <BLOCKS>` — Ids this item blocks — comma-separated or repeatable.
* `--links <LINKS>` — Ids this item is associated with (its plan, proposal, …) — comma-separated or repeatable.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Epic name — the delivery grouping this item belongs to (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Milestone name — the target this item ships under (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).

* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Estimate in points (0–1000) — relative size, not hours.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Cycle name — the iteration this item is scheduled in (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`).

## `myco item`

Kind-agnostic item verbs — show / set / move.

**Usage:** `myco item <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `show` — Dump items — frontmatter fields, kind-grouped related edges (blocks/blocked_by/supersedes/associated/references/handoff, live-derived), plus the body for file-backed kinds (`--json` = the full Item + location + related + body). 1..n ids: a batch repeats the block in argument order; `--json` emits the per-id `[{id, ok, …}]` array.
* `set` — Mutate an item in place. `--status` is the only field routed through the state machine — single steps only, invalid ones error with the valid targets. Status changes on tasks move the line between TODO.md and BACKLOG.md (`done` archives the subtree into DONE.md — terminal, so it confirms on a tty: `--yes`/`$MYCO_YES` skips).
* `move` — Move an item to another repo's ledger — re-creates it in the destination's own id sequence (kind, title, body, pri/owner/labels/epic/milestone carried; `blocks:`/`links:` dropped — they name source-ledger ids), writes a `moved from`/`moved to` provenance handoff on both sides, then walks the source to `done` (a task's line leaves the ledger; its handoff drops to `handoffs/archive/`). `--to` takes the destination repo root, its `project/` worktree, or a registered repo name (`myco index list`). Two commits — one per worktree.

## `myco item show`

Dump items — frontmatter fields, kind-grouped related edges (blocks/blocked_by/supersedes/associated/references/handoff, live-derived), plus the body for file-backed kinds (`--json` = the full Item + location + related + body). 1..n ids: a batch repeats the block in argument order; `--json` emits the per-id `[{id, ok, …}]` array.

**Usage:** `myco item show <id>...`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Any item id (`T-NNN`, `I-NNN`, `P-NNN`, `ADR-NNNN`, `PL-NNN`) — live or archived.

## `myco item set`

Mutate an item in place. `--status` is the only field routed through the state machine — single steps only, invalid ones error with the valid targets. Status changes on tasks move the line between TODO.md and BACKLOG.md (`done` archives the subtree into DONE.md — terminal, so it confirms on a tty: `--yes`/`$MYCO_YES` skips).

**Usage:** `myco item set [OPTIONS] <id>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Any item id.

###### **Options:**

* `--status <STATUS>` — New status — one legal step from the current one.
* `--pri <PRI>` \[alias: `priority`] — Priority: low|med|high|crit.
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor id.
* `--label <LABEL>` — Add (`+x` or `x`) or remove (`-x`) a label — repeatable.
* `--unlabel <UNLABEL>` — Remove a label — repeatable.
* `--blocks <BLOCKS>` — Add (`+T-1` or `T-1`) or remove (`-T-1`) a blocks dep — repeatable or comma-separated.
* `--unblock <UNBLOCK>` — Remove a blocks dep — repeatable or comma-separated.
* `--links <LINKS>` — Add (`+PL-1` or `PL-1`) or remove (`-PL-1`) a link — repeatable or comma-separated.
* `--unlink <UNLINK>` — Remove a link — repeatable or comma-separated.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Epic name — `""` clears the epic.
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Milestone name — `""` clears the milestone.
* `--due <DUE>` — Due date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) — `""` clears the due date.
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Estimate in points (0–1000) — `""` clears the estimate.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Cycle name (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`) — `""` clears the cycle.
* `--session <SESSION>` — Tag the item's claim with a session id — appends a `claimed` handoff entry carrying it (`interrupt --session` scopes teardown to it). The item must land in a work state.
* `--yes` — Skip the `--status done` confirmation prompt (also `$MYCO_YES`; non-interactive runs never prompt).

## `myco item move`

Move an item to another repo's ledger — re-creates it in the destination's own id sequence (kind, title, body, pri/owner/labels/epic/milestone carried; `blocks:`/`links:` dropped — they name source-ledger ids), writes a `moved from`/`moved to` provenance handoff on both sides, then walks the source to `done` (a task's line leaves the ledger; its handoff drops to `handoffs/archive/`). `--to` takes the destination repo root, its `project/` worktree, or a registered repo name (`myco index list`). Two commits — one per worktree.

**Usage:** `myco item move [OPTIONS] --to <to> <id>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Any item id.

###### **Options:**

* `--to <TO>` — Destination — a repo root, its `project/` worktree, or a registered repo name.
* `--note <NOTE>` — Extra context appended to the source's `moved to` handoff note.
* `--actor <ACTOR>` — Who moved it (default `cli`).
* `--yes` — Skip the confirmation prompt (also `$MYCO_YES`; non-interactive runs never prompt).

## `myco absorb`

Import work into the ledger — TODO/FIXME comments, Jira CSV exports, GitHub issue dumps.

**Usage:** `myco absorb <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `comments` — Sweep code comments into the ledger via ripgrep (`rg` must be installed — respects `.gitignore`; `project/`, `docs/`, `target/` are excluded).
* `jira` — Import a Jira CSV export. `Done`/`Resolved` rows are skipped unless `--include-done` (created done + archived).
* `github` — Import a GitHub issues dump — a JSON array (`number`, `title`, `state`, `labels`, `assignee`, `body`) or the CSV equivalent. `closed` rows are skipped unless `--include-done` (created done + archived).

## `myco absorb comments`

Sweep code comments into the ledger via ripgrep (`rg` must be installed — respects `.gitignore`; `project/`, `docs/`, `target/` are excluded).

**Usage:** `myco absorb comments [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--path <PATH>` — Directory to scan (default: the repo root).
* `--kinds <KINDS>` — Comment kinds to match — comma-separated or repeatable (default TODO,FIXME,HACK).
* `--to <TO>` — Where findings land: `backlog` items or `issues` files (default `backlog`).

  Default value: `backlog`
* `--dry` — Report findings without creating items or committing.

## `myco absorb jira`

Import a Jira CSV export. `Done`/`Resolved` rows are skipped unless `--include-done` (created done + archived).

**Usage:** `myco absorb jira [OPTIONS] <file>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<FILE>` — The export file (`.csv`).

###### **Options:**

* `--include-done` — Import done/resolved issues too.

## `myco absorb github`

Import a GitHub issues dump — a JSON array (`number`, `title`, `state`, `labels`, `assignee`, `body`) or the CSV equivalent. `closed` rows are skipped unless `--include-done` (created done + archived).

**Usage:** `myco absorb github [OPTIONS] <file>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<FILE>` — The export file (`.json` or `.csv`).

###### **Options:**

* `--include-done` — Import closed issues too.

## `myco index`

The derived index: register repos, query/rebuild snapshots.

**Usage:** `myco index <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `add` — Register a repo — `<path>` is a repo root (or its `project/` worktree). Ledger-less repos register as `ledger = "none"` with no snapshot; `--org` marks the org/global ledger.
* `remove` — Unregister a repo and drop its snapshot.
* `list` — List registered repos with snapshot freshness.
* `rebuild` — Re-scan a registered repo (all of them without `<path>`).

## `myco index add`

Register a repo — `<path>` is a repo root (or its `project/` worktree). Ledger-less repos register as `ledger = "none"` with no snapshot; `--org` marks the org/global ledger.

**Usage:** `myco index add [OPTIONS] <path>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>` — Repo root (or project worktree) to register.

###### **Options:**

* `--org` — Designate this repo as the org/global ledger — the fallback target verbs in ledger-less registered repos resolve to (at most one; clears the mark elsewhere).

## `myco index remove`

Unregister a repo and drop its snapshot.

**Usage:** `myco index remove <path>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>` — Registered repo root (or project worktree).

## `myco index list`

List registered repos with snapshot freshness.

**Usage:** `myco index list`

## `myco index rebuild`

Re-scan a registered repo (all of them without `<path>`).

**Usage:** `myco index rebuild [path]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<PATH>` — Registered repo root (or project worktree).

## `myco org`

**Usage:** `myco org <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `init` — Re-run `init` on every registered repo — refreshes the worktree scaffold and root files (.gitignore, the AGENTS.md agent-awareness block). The rollout path for new scaffolding.

## `myco org init`

Re-run `init` on every registered repo — refreshes the worktree scaffold and root files (.gitignore, the AGENTS.md agent-awareness block). The rollout path for new scaffolding.

**Usage:** `myco org init`

## `myco schema`

The file/state spec, machine-readable JSON Schema.

**Usage:** `myco schema`

## `myco init`

Scaffold `project/`: orphan branch + worktree + .gitignore + seed files + the managed AGENTS.md agent-awareness block. Idempotent — existing worktree and AGENTS.md prose are preserved, only the marked block is (re)written.

**Usage:** `myco init`

## `myco check`

Validate the ledger (schemas, state machine, ids, refs) and the worktree it lives in (detached HEAD, wrong branch, unpushed commits); also validates the managed AGENTS.md block on the repo root. Findings carry a severity: `error` exits 1, `warning` is reported and costs nothing (ADR-0002). `--fix` applies safe repairs + commits, including reattaching a detached worktree.

**Usage:** `myco check [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--fix` — Repair drift in place instead of only reporting.

## `myco migrate`

Convert legacy ledgers to v2: `pm/` → `project/`, or normalize files already on the `project` branch.

**Usage:** `myco migrate`

## `myco commit`

Stage + commit worktree changes (conventional message).

**Usage:** `myco commit [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `-m`, `--message <MESSAGE>` — Commit message (default: `chore: update project ledger`).

## `myco undo`

Undo the last ledger commit — resets the `project` branch tip one back (`HEAD~1`). One verb = one commit, so the reset is the inverse mutation, file deletions included; the undone commit is journaled for `redo`. Refuses on a dirty worktree (uncommitted `--no-commit` writes), at the root commit, and when the tip is already published on `origin` (unless `--force`). `--list` shows the redoable stack without mutating.

**Usage:** `myco undo [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--force` — Undo even when the tip commit is already published on the remote.
* `--list` — List the redoable commits (newest first) instead of undoing.

## `myco redo`

Redo the last undo — pops the undo journal and restores the commit `myco undo` moved away from (`git reset --hard <target>`). Repeatable while entries remain; the stack self-invalidates when the ledger moves (any commit/pull/manual git op since the undo). Refuses on a dirty worktree.

**Usage:** `myco redo`

## `myco sync`

Reconcile the ledger branch with `origin/<branch>` — fetch, fast-forward or rebase local commits onto the remote tip, then heal merge damage: `meta.toml` counters reconcile, duplicate ids renumber remote-wins (the pushed item keeps its id; the local one moves, refs stay bound to the remote). Mutating verbs refuse while behind (`ensure_synced`), so this is the gate. A rebase conflict stops mid-flight — resolve + `git rebase --continue` + `myco sync` again, or `--abort` to bail.

**Usage:** `myco sync [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--abort` — Abort a stopped rebase/merge (`git rebase --abort`) and return to the pre-sync tip.

## `myco view`

Declarative views — named presets (`[views.<name>]` in config + built-ins `board|open|epic|milestone|next`, plus index-sourced `org-board|org-status` for cross-repo) or an ad-hoc spec from flags (`--source index` unions the registered repos' snapshots). `myco view board` is the kanban; `format = "repos"` emits one row per repo; bare `myco view` lists views (or renders `default_view` when config names one).

**Usage:** `myco view [OPTIONS] [name]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>` — View name — builtin preset or config view.

###### **Options:**

* `--list` — List defined views and exit.
* `--md` — Emit a markdown table (board/repos formats).
* `--all` — Show every row — no cap.
* `--kind <KIND>` — Item kinds — task|issue|proposal|adr|plan (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--status <STATUS>` — Statuses — open|claimed|in-progress|blocked|done|deferred (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--pri-min <PRI_MIN>` — Inclusive lower severity bound — low|med|high|crit.
* `--pri-max <PRI_MAX>` — Inclusive upper severity bound.
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#`-less label — item carries any of these (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor — item's owner is any of these (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--claimed` — Items with an owner.
* `--unclaimed` — Items with no owner.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Items in this epic.
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Items in this milestone.
* `--due <DUE>` — Items due on this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Items with this point estimate.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Items in this cycle.
* `--live-only` — Items not superseded by another (ADRs).
* `--superseded` — Items superseded by another (ADRs).
* `--source <SOURCE>` — Item universe — repo (default) reads this worktree; index unions every registered repo's snapshot (org views).
* `--group-by <GROUP_BY>` — Group axis — status|priority|kind|owner|epic|milestone|repo.
* `--sort <SORT>` — Sort keys — `pri,id,-created`; `-` flips a key's default direction.
* `--limit <N>` — Keep the first N items after sorting.
* `--format <FORMAT>` — Renderer — list|board|repos.

## `myco next`

The single highest-priority open item — "what should I work on" (a `view` eval with limit 1: open tasks+issues, `pri,id`; the filter flags merge over that default). `--claim` mutates it to `claimed` + an owner in one commit.

**Usage:** `myco next [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--kind <KIND>` — Item kinds — task|issue|proposal|adr|plan (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--status <STATUS>` — Statuses — open|claimed|in-progress|blocked|done|deferred (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--pri-min <PRI_MIN>` — Inclusive lower severity bound — low|med|high|crit.
* `--pri-max <PRI_MAX>` — Inclusive upper severity bound.
* `--label <LABEL>` — `#`-less label — item carries any of these (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--owner <OWNER>` — Owner actor — item's owner is any of these (repeatable/comma-separated).
* `--claimed` — Items with an owner.
* `--unclaimed` — Items with no owner.
* `--epic <EPIC>` — Items in this epic.
* `--milestone <MILESTONE>` — Items in this milestone.
* `--due <DUE>` — Items due on this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
* `--est <EST>` \[alias: `estimate`] — Items with this point estimate.
* `--cycle <CYCLE>` — Items in this cycle.
* `--live-only` — Items not superseded by another (ADRs).
* `--superseded` — Items superseded by another (ADRs).
* `--sort <SORT>` — Sort keys — `pri,id,-created`; `-` flips a key's default direction. Default `pri,id`.
* `--claim` — Claim the emitted item — status `claimed`, owner set to the `--owner` actor (else `cli`); `--owner` names the claimer here and doesn't filter. Mutating: one commit.
* `--session <SESSION>` — With `--claim`: tag the claim with a session id — appends a `claimed` handoff entry carrying it (`interrupt --session` scopes teardown to it).

## `myco status`

Cheap digest of the work ledger. `--prompt` = token-sized.

**Usage:** `myco status [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--prompt` — Render for an agent prompt (minimal tokens).

## `myco report`

Aging + velocity + blocked — how the ledger is trending.

**Usage:** `myco report`

## `myco handoff`

Attach resumable state at session end — appends a dated entry to `handoffs/<ID>.md` (any item kind, live or archived; append-only).

**Usage:** `myco handoff [OPTIONS] --note <TEXT|-> <id>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Any item id (`T-NNN`, `I-NNN`, `P-NNN`, `ADR-NNNN`, `PL-NNN`).

###### **Options:**

* `--note <TEXT|->` — Handoff note — done/next/open. `-` reads stdin.
* `--actor <ACTOR>` — Who wrote it (`devin`, `human:luis`, …; default `cli`).
* `--session <SESSION>` — Session provenance — a sepia session id, `cli:<pid>`, any id string.

## `myco interrupt`

A session ended with work still claimed/in-progress/blocked — revert the item to `open` + `interrupted` handoff, one commit. Without an id, `--session <id>` is the teardown: every item claimed under that session reverts in one commit. Session-lifecycle hooks (sepia, CLI session-end) call this; myco never detects sessions itself.

**Usage:** `myco interrupt [OPTIONS] [id]`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Any item id (`T-NNN`, `I-NNN`, `P-NNN`, `ADR-NNNN`, `PL-NNN`) — omit for the `--session` bulk teardown.

###### **Options:**

* `--note <TEXT>` — Extra context appended to the `interrupted` note.
* `--actor <ACTOR>` — Who interrupted it (default `cli`).
* `--session <SESSION>` — Session scope — a sepia session id, `cli:<pid>`, any id string. With `id`: interrupt only when the item's claim tag matches. Without `id`: teardown — interrupt every item claimed under it.

## `myco resume`

Minimal context block to restart work on an item — the item, `blocks:` dep titles, latest handoffs, open checklist. The single-item `status --prompt`. 1..n ids batch in one call.

**Usage:** `myco resume [OPTIONS] <id>...`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<ID>` — Any item id (`T-NNN`, `I-NNN`, `P-NNN`, `ADR-NNNN`, `PL-NNN`) — live or archived.

###### **Options:**

* `--last <LAST>` — Only the latest N handoff entries (default 10).

## `myco ui`

Interactive board TUI (ratatui) — TODO/BACKLOG tabs, item preview, writes through the same ops the verbs use; auto-reloads when the ledger changes on disk. `--view` with a `source = "index"` spec (org-\*) opens the cross-repo index board: `repo:ID` rows, verbs write the owning repo.

**Usage:** `myco ui [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--view <NAME>` — Open with a named view's filter narrowing every board; index-sourced views load the cross-repo universe.

## `myco serve`

Sequential request/response verb surface on stdio — JSON-RPC 2.0, one line in / one line out. For embedding (peregrin spawns one per repo); stdin IS the wire, so no served method reads content from it.

**Usage:** `myco serve`

## `myco batch`

One-shot `serve` — NDJSON verb requests from stdin or `--file`, one JSON-RPC response line per request, dispatched through the same served surface. Per-line errors never fail the run; mutations keep per-request commits (`--no-commit`/`$MYCO_NO_COMMIT` apply). stdin IS the wire here too — requests that would read it are rejected.

**Usage:** `myco batch [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--file <PATH>` — Read NDJSON requests from this file instead of stdin.

clap-markdown.&#xA;

# Config — `myco.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project_dir` | `string` | optional | Path to the project worktree, relative to the repo root. |
| `default_view` | `string` | optional | The named view bare `myco view` resolves when no name is given — a repo pins its landing view, a machine `~/myco.toml` pins a global one (scalar: repo layer wins). |
| `views` | `map` | optional | Named declarative views — merged across config layers (P-006): repo `myco.toml` presets are shared, user-config presets personal; the *user* layer wins a name collision. |
| `verbs` | `map` | optional | Config-declared verbs (P-007) — merged like `views`, but the *repo* layer wins collisions (repo verbs are shared surface, personal verbs don't override them). Builtins win over both at resolution. |
| `kinds` | `Vec<KindSpec>` | optional | `[[kinds]]` — user item kinds layered over the prelude (P-008). A prelude name *shadows* that spec (prefix stays locked); new names extend the table. Merged like verbs: the repo layer wins a name collision — a repo's kind vocabulary is shared surface. |

## Constraints

* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.
* Search order: `$MYCO_CONFIG` → `./myco.toml` →
  `~/.config/myco/myco.toml`. The file is optional — no
  `myco.toml` anywhere just means defaults.

# Managed `AGENTS.md` blocks

The `<tool>:agent-awareness` convention — how multiple tools each
maintain a section of a repo's `AGENTS.md` without clobbering human
prose or each other. Normative; **myco is the reference
implementation** (`crates/myco-cli/src/agentmd.rs`). The sturn
and kuda blocks in the sibling 9aia repos are deployed against
it.

Keywords **MUST** / **MUST NOT** / **SHOULD** / **MAY** read as in
RFC 2119.

## Purpose

`AGENTS.md` at the repo root is agent-facing operating
instructions. Each participating tool owns exactly one
marker-delimited block; everything outside markers is human-owned
and untouchable. A tool's init writes its block, its check
verifies it, and syncs are idempotent — safe to re-run forever.

## The block

```markdown
<!-- <tool>:agent-awareness -->

## <Tool> awareness

- <tool-specific bullets>

<!-- /<tool>:agent-awareness -->
```

* `<tool>` is the implementer's canonical lowercase name (`myco`,
  `sturn`, `kuda`…). The marker pair is the ownership boundary —
  everything between them MAY be rewritten by the owning tool at
  any time.
* Markers **MUST** sit on their own lines. Detection tolerates
  leading/trailing whitespace; canonical emission has none.
* The section heading **SHOULD** be `## <Tool> awareness` —
  uniqueness across tools is what matters (see *upgrade* below).
* Block content is tool-internal: markers are the contract, the
  prose inside is the tool's own business.

## Ownership

* A tool **MUST** rewrite only inside its own marker pair.
* All other content — human prose and foreign tools' marked
  blocks — is opaque: preserved verbatim, never reordered, never
  merged, never reformatted.
* Blocks coexist in any order. A new block appends at end of
  file; a tool **MUST NOT** move its own or others' blocks.
* A tool **MUST NOT** emit a second marker pair, emit markers
  inside foreign blocks, or leave stray markers behind.

## Sync

The write path (`init`, `check --fix`, any rollout) applies one
merge:

1. **Own complete marker pair** → replace the span
   `[BEGIN … END]` inclusive with the canonical block.
2. **No intact pair** → drop stray own-markers; if the file holds
   the tool's claimed heading (an *unmarked* `## <Tool>
   awareness` section), replace that section through the next
   heading of the same-or-higher level — the upgrade path for
   pre-convention or hand-written content.
3. **Neither** → append the canonical block at end of file.

Emission rules:

* Exactly one blank line on each side of the block.
* File ends with exactly one newline.
* Bytes outside the block survive byte-for-byte — no other
  whitespace normalization.
* Sync of already-canonical input is a **no-op** (no write) —
  this is what makes it idempotent.

## States & `check --fix`

Every implementation exposes the same four-state read:

| state | meaning | `check --fix` |
|---|---|---|
| `missing` | no `AGENTS.md` | creates file + block |
| `absent` | file exists, nothing block-shaped | appends block |
| `drift` | stray markers, handwritten section, or non-canonical content | rewrites to canonical |
| `ok` | canonical | no finding, no write |

`check` **MUST** surface non-`ok` as a fixable finding. Detection
is a simulated sync: markers present and `sync(content) ==
content` (modulo the trailing newline) → `ok`.

## Multi-tool coexistence

* Foreign marked regions are opaque to *all* of a tool's logic —
  including its upgrade scan. When looking for its claimed
  heading, a tool skips headings inside other tools' marker
  pairs.
* The `## <Tool> awareness` naming rule is what prevents upgrade
  collisions: two tools scanning the same unmarked file must
  claim different headings.
* Deployed blocks may interleave with prose arbitrarily — no tool
  may assume adjacency or ordering.

## Deployment

* Writes happen on the repo's checked-out branch (the block lives
  beside `AGENTS.md`, not on any tool-owned branch), committed
  separately from other init artifacts. myco's message:
  `chore: manage AGENTS.md agent-awareness block`.
* Multi-repo rollout is an implementer concern (myco: `myco org
  init` applies the block across registered repos).

## Implementation notes

* myco's deployed heading is `## Agent awareness` — predates the
  `<Tool> awareness` rule; it is the one allowed exception, and
  its upgrade matcher is deliberately scoped to that heading so
  no other tool can accidentally adopt it.
* myco exposes the state over the wire: `check --json` reports
  `agents_md: missing|absent|drift|ok` alongside the finding.

url: /myco/explanation/worktree-model.md
---
# The worktree model

Why `project/` is a git worktree of an orphan branch — and what
that buys you.

## The shape

```text
your-repo/
├── src/ …            ← code branch (main)
├── project/          ← worktree of the orphan `project` branch
│   ├── TODO.md
│   ├── BACKLOG.md
│   ├── DONE.md
│   ├── issues/  proposals/  plans/  adrs/  handoffs/
│   ├── index.md
│   └── meta.toml
└── .gitignore        ← gains `project/`
```

The `project` branch shares the repo's `.git` object store but
has disjoint history — an orphan root, no code ancestors. The
worktree mounts it as a plain directory, so tools see ordinary
files while `git worktree list` shows the truth.

## Why an orphan branch

PM state moves at its own cadence. On an orphan branch, ledger
commits never touch the code history: no `chore: defer T-009`
noise in `main`'s log, no PM diffs in PRs, no branch protection
friction. `project/` is gitignored on every code branch — the
worktree physically can't leak into a code commit.

## Why a worktree (not just a branch)

The ledger has to be *visible* — agents edit files, humans read
`TODO.md` — without `git checkout` swapping the code tree. A
worktree keeps both checked out at once.

## Commits are the audit trail

Every mutating verb is one atomic, conventional commit on
`project` (`chore: add T-012`, `chore: handoff T-012`,
`chore: resolve I-003`, …). So
`git -C project log` *is* the history of intent — who moved what
when, replayable and greppable, with no separate audit store.
`--no-commit` / `$MYCO_NO_COMMIT` opts out per run; `myco commit`
squashes a batch into one. `myco undo` rewinds the tip one commit
(`HEAD~1`) — the exact inverse of the last verb — refusing dirty
worktrees, the root commit, and published tips unless `--force`.
Each undo is journaled in `<git-common-dir>/myco-history.json` —
a small stack of undone commits, each anchored on the HEAD it was
undone from — and `myco redo` pops it (`git reset --hard <target>`),
repeatable while entries remain. The stack self-invalidates: any
commit, pull, or manual git op breaks the anchor and clears it.
The journal is derived state — corrupt or missing reads as empty,
never an error — and lives outside `project/`, so it is never
committed to the ledger.

That sentence is only true while the worktree is attached. A
`project/` worktree on a **detached HEAD** commits onto no branch:
the files change, the trail does not. So the invariant is enforced
rather than assumed (ADR-0003):

* `myco check` reports `worktree-detached` as an **error**
  (`worktree-branch` and `worktree-unpushed` are warnings), and
  `myco check --fix` reattaches with `git checkout -B project`,
  keeping the detached commits as the branch tip.
* Every mutating verb refuses a detached ledger before writing —
  the error names the repair.
* `myco check` never pushes. `worktree-unpushed` is a warning
  because local-only is a legitimate mode (offline, no remote,
  pre-publication); publishing is `git push origin project` or
  sturn's business.

## Canonical markdown, disposable index

The markdown in `project/` is canonical — human-editable,
diffable, frozen by golden fixtures. The redb index
(`index.redb` + `repos.toml` under `$MYCO_HOME` →
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/myco` → `~/.local/share/myco`) is a *derived
cache* that powers `status`, `view`, `report`, and `org` without
re-parsing files. Delete it and `myco index rebuild` derives it
back; `myco check` finds and repairs drift between the two.

See [the file spec](file-spec.md) for what the files contain and
[architecture](architecture.md) for the crates that implement it.
