url: /myco/explanation/file-spec.md
---
# The ledger file spec

What `project/` contains, how items are written, and the state
machine they live under. `myco schema` emits all of this as
machine-readable JSON Schema; `myco check` enforces it.

## Layout

| path         | holds                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `meta.toml`  | `name` + `[next]` per-kind id counters (`t`, `i`, `p`, `adr`, `pl`) |
| `TODO.md`    | open-line tasks (`T-`), `##` sections, nested children              |
| `BACKLOG.md` | deferred items — same grammar, no checkbox                          |
| `DONE.md`    | done archive — same grammar, status pinned `done`                   |
| `index.md`   | free-form human index — verbatim, never rewritten                   |
| `issues/`    | `issue-NNNN-<slug>.md` + `issues/archive/`                          |
| `proposals/` | `proposal-NNNN-<slug>.md` + `proposals/archive/`                    |
| `plans/`     | `pl-NNNN-<slug>.md` + `plans/archive/`                              |
| `adrs/`      | `NNNN-<slug>.md` + `adrs/archive/`                                  |
| `handoffs/`  | `<ID>.md` append-only + `handoffs/archive/`                         |

## Item ids

`<prefix>-<number>`, zero-padded per kind: `T-001` tasks,
`I-001` issues, `P-001` proposals, `PL-001` plans, `ADR-0001`
ADRs. One registry, per-kind counters in `meta.toml`'s `[next]`
table — ids are never reused. Tasks live as lines; the four
file-backed kinds (`I`, `P`, `PL`, `ADR`) get a markdown file
each, filenames padded to four digits.

## Line items — TODO.md / BACKLOG.md / DONE.md

```markdown
# TODO — <repo>

## <section>

- [ ] T-012 <title> · status:in-progress · pri:high · owner:devin · created:2026-10-29 · #label · blocks:I-001 · links:PL-001,P-013 · epic:v2 · ms:1.0 · due:2026-12-01 · est:3 · cycle:sprint-12 · note:<text>
  - [ ] T-013 a sub-task — children are the same grammar, indented 2 spaces/level
```

* `BACKLOG.md` lines are the same shape minus `[ ]`, default
  status `deferred`; `TODO.md` defaults to `open`. `DONE.md` is
  the done archive — same line grammar, status pinned `done`,
  read by `myco done list` and still resolvable via
  `myco item show`.
* `done` moves the line (subtree included) to `DONE.md` —
  completed work stays visible instead of vanishing;
  `defer` moves it to `BACKLOG.md`; `promote` moves it back.
* `done`/`defer` on a parent act on the whole subtree; on a
  child, just that node.
* Token order is canonical (`status`, `pri`, `owner`, `created`,
  `#label`, `blocks`, `links`, `epic`, `ms`, `due`, `est`, `cycle`,
  `note`) so emit produces minimal diffs. `ms` is the milestone
  token — kept short. `links:` declares kind-agnostic associations
  — the plan, proposal, or ADR an item belongs to (`myco item set --links` / `--unlink`). `due` is a `YYYY-MM-DD` date, `est` a
  point estimate (0–1000, `--est`/`--estimate`), `cycle` an
  iteration name — the scheduling trio (`due`/`estimate`/`cycle`
  in file frontmatter).
* Patterns: actors `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`, labels `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`,
  epic/ms/cycle names `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`, priority
  `low|med|high|crit`.

## File items — issues/ proposals/ plans/ adrs/

`+++` TOML frontmatter + free-form markdown body:

```markdown
+++
id = "P-001"
title = "myco v2 — agent-first project management, in Rust"
status = "open"
created = "2026-10-29"
priority = "med"
labels = ["design"]
blocks = ["T-008"]
links = ["PL-001", "P-013"]
epic = "v2"
milestone = "1.0"
due = "2026-12-01"
estimate = 3
cycle = "sprint-12"
+++

# Title

Body — templates seed Context/Decision/Consequences-shaped
sections per kind.
```

Frontmatter keys: `id`, `title`, `status`, `created`, `owner`,
`priority`, `labels`, `blocks`, `links`, `note`, `superseded_by`,
`supersedes`, `epic`, `milestone`, `due`, `estimate`, `cycle`.
`priority` spells the `pri:`
token (`low|med|high|crit`) — the serde full names `medium` /
`critical` still read but re-emit as tokens on any write. `due`
is a `YYYY-MM-DD` string (a bare TOML date reads the same and
re-emits quoted), `estimate` a 0–1000 point count, `cycle` a
name — unknown keys are ignored on read (forward-compat) and
dropped on re-emit.
Archiving moves the file to `<dir>/archive/` — `myco item show`
still finds archived items.

## State machine

Six statuses; `item set --status` and kind verbs walk it one
legal step at a time:

| from          | can go to                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `open`        | `claimed`, `in-progress`, `deferred` |
| `claimed`     | `in-progress`, `open`, `deferred`    |
| `in-progress` | `blocked`, `done`, `deferred`, `open` |
| `blocked`     | `in-progress`, `open`, `deferred`    |
| `deferred`    | `open`                               |
| `done`        | — (terminal)                         |

Proposal words alias the machine: `draft` = `open`, `accepted` =
`done`, `rejected` = `deferred` — the transition still walks the
graph (`accepted` passes `open → in-progress → done`). ADR status
`open` reads as "proposed"; `adr supersede` closes the old file
with `superseded_by:` and stamps the replacement `supersedes:`.

## Handoffs

`handoffs/<ID>.md` — one file per item, uniform across kinds:

```markdown
+++
item = "T-012"
+++

# Handoffs — T-012

## 2026-10-29 · devin · session:cli:abc123

Done: parser. Next: emitter. Open: archive semantics.
```

Append-only: every `myco handoff` is one `##` entry + one commit;
entries are never rewritten. When an item's file goes away, its
handoff file is orphaned — `myco check` reports it and
`check --fix` moves it to `handoffs/archive/`, where `resume`
still finds it.

---

---
url: /myco/explanation/architecture.md
---
# Architecture

Ports-and-adapters over a flat `crates/` workspace:
`myco-core` is pure domain — item models, the id registry, the
state machine — with no I/O. Ports are traits (`myco-store`,
`myco-config`, `myco-index`); impls live in separate crates;
`crates/myco-cli` (package `myco`) is the composition root that
wires impls to verbs.

Design rules:

* **No `unsafe`, no async** — the binary stays dependency-light
  and synchronous; no runtime to embed.
* **Git via the `git` CLI** — `myco-git` shells out for the
  orphan branch, worktree, and per-verb commits; no
  libgit2/gix binding.
* **Markdown is the file spec** — `myco-store-md` owns strict
  parse/emit: deterministic output, stable ordering, minimal
  diffs. `myco-testkit` freezes emit with golden fixtures and
  proptest round-trips, so the format can't drift silently.
* **The index is derived, never canonical** — `myco-index-redb`
  snapshots ledgers into redb for `status`/`view`/`org`; it can
  be deleted and rebuilt at any time.

| crate | layer | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `myco-core` | domain | myco domain core: item models, ID registry, state machine — pure, no I/O |
| `myco-config` | port | Config port: where myco.toml-shaped config comes from |
| `myco-index` | port | Index port: the derived, disposable cache powering status/board/report/org views |
| `myco-store` | port | Store port: where project/ state (TODO.md, BACKLOG.md, meta.toml, item files) is persisted |
| `myco-ops` | ops | myco — ops I/O shell: project discovery, store open/save, commit-per-mutation, verb plumbing |
| `myco-config-toml` | adapter | Config impl: myco.toml file (explicit path, env, ./, ~/.config) |
| `myco-driver` | adapter | tamias-driver-myco — pavo view driver over a repo's project/ ledger (reads via myco-ops) |
| `myco-git` | adapter | Git plumbing for myco — shells out to the git CLI; owns the project branch/worktree mechanics |
| `myco-index-redb` | adapter | Index impl: redb snapshots + repos.toml registry under ~/.local/share/myco (disposable derived cache) |
| `myco-shell` | adapter | Run a command in a working directory via bash -c — the generic shell-out helper |
| `myco-store-md` | adapter | Markdown adapter for the store port — strict parse/emit of project/ files, round-trip stable; owns the file spec |
| `myco-testkit` | adapter | Golden fixtures + conformance: frozen md emit snapshots and proptest round-trips for the project/ file spec |
| `myco-tui` | adapter | myco — interactive board TUI (ratatui); a thin front-end over myco-ops |
| `myco` | binary | myco — agent-first project management; a records + views + mutations engine, PM is the shipped prelude |

## The engine and the prelude

The shape that emerged rather than being designed: **myco is a
records + views + mutations engine, and PM is its shipped prelude**
(P-009). `myco init` seeds that prelude — the five `[[kinds]]`, the
builtin views, the registry verbs — so editing config isn't
customizing a PM tool, it's programming an engine whose default
program happens to be project management.

```text
            engine (code)                      prelude (seeded config)
  ┌────────────────────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │ sources   repo │ index         │    │ [[kinds]]  task issue …       │
  │ eval      filter→group→sort    │    │ [views]    board open hot …   │
  │ emits     list board md json   │    │ [verbs]    alias view-emit …  │
  │ dispatch  one registry table   │    └───────────────────────────────┘
  └────────────────────────────────┘
      owns, must never be data            declared, layered, shadowable
```

The crate is also a library: `myco-cli`'s `lib.rs` exposes
`parse_from`/`run_from`/`dispatch` so `myco-driver` (and any
embedder) drives the same engine in-process — `src/main.rs` is a
six-line compat bin over it.

A read is `universe → eval → emit`:

| stage | knob | values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| universe | `source` | `repo` (this worktree) · `index` (the registered-repo union) |
| eval | `filter → group_by → sort → limit` | a `ViewSpec`, from config or flags |
| emit | `format` | `list` · `board` · `repos` (`--md` / `--json` are output modifiers, not spec values) |

Every feature gets asked one question — **engine or prelude?**
Engine answers generalize (a new source, axis or format); prelude
answers configure (which kinds, views and verbs ship seeded).

### What stays code

The moat is what must be *owned* rather than declared: the markdown
file spec, atomic commit-per-mutation on `project`, the state
machine, the id registry. `Item` keeps fixed semantics — a schema
DSL over arbitrary fields would make this jq-over-markdown, a
different and worse product. Mutations stay code as well: the
prelude configures *what* exists, never *how* writes behave
(ADR-0004, one registry).

## Boundary — work memory only

myco owns the ledger of intent (tasks, issues, proposals, plans,
ADRs, handoffs). Neighbors own their own memory:

* **sturn** — ephemeral coordination (live claims/ops/topics)
* **kuda** — code memory; myco indexes work items, not code
* **peregrin** — orchestration; it embeds the ledger through
  `myco serve` (JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio — `adrs/0001`), reachable
  one-shot via `myco batch`
* **bupha** — CI gate (was: `myco check` in pipelines,
  `Item:` trailers); bupha is the CI repo again — the org gate is
  mid-migration back from the peregrin `ci-gate` campaign (PL-013)
* **mycena** — surfaces TODO/FIXME in code → `myco absorb`
* **sepia** — session lifecycle → `myco handoff` / `myco resume`

Anything needing a daemon, a multi-machine view, or arbitration
between actors belongs to peregrin, not here.

---

---
url: /myco/explanation/release-model.md
---
# Release model

Releases are manual: `scripts/release.sh` is run by an operator
on `main`. The script's
leading debounce window (default 5 min, `MYCO_RELEASE_DEBOUNCE`)
still applies, and it pushes commits and tags to `main`.

## What a release run does

1. **Diff since the last tag** — the release set is a *fixed*
   list of six crates: `myco-core`, `myco-git`, `myco-config`,
   `myco-config-toml`, `myco-shell`, `myco-cli`. Only changes
   under `crates/<one-of-those>/` count; changes to `myco-ops`,
   `myco-store*`, `myco-index*`, `myco-tui`, `myco-driver`, or
   `myco-testkit` trigger nothing. The `myco` binary re-publishes
   whenever any of the six changed. No release-set changes, no
   release.
2. **Per-crate patch bump + publish** —
   `cargo set-version -p <crate> --bump patch`, then
   `cargo publish` with retries, in dependency order
   (`myco-core myco-config myco-git myco-shell myco-config-toml
   myco`).
   Each crate gets its own tag `<crate>-v<ver>` — versions
   diverge independently in the monorepo.
3. **Commit + push** — one `release: bump crate versions` commit,
   pushed to `main` with the tags.
4. **Binary dist** — when `dist` and `gh` are available, a local
   `dist build` produces the shell installer
   (`dist-workspace.toml`, host arch `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
   only — other targets are a TODO for remote workers), uploaded
   to a GitHub Release `myco-v<ver>` with generated notes.

With no tags at all the script exits early — the flow is seeded
by tagging once.

## Constraints

* The crates.io name `myco` is currently held by an unrelated
  project, so `cargo publish` of the CLI package depends on
  resolving that; installs should use
  `cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco` regardless.
* Only the six release-set crates publish — the rest of the
  workspace (`myco-ops`, `myco-store*`, `myco-index*`, `myco-tui`,
  `myco-driver`, `myco-testkit`) is internal and installs via
  `cargo install --git`.

## CI and docs deploys

There are no GitHub Actions workflows; the gate is the peregrin
`ci-gate` campaign (the gate is mid-migration back to bupha):

* **Push to `docs`** runs `scripts/deploy-docs.sh`, which
  rebuilds the site and pushes `gh-pages` — Pages is a legacy
  branch deploy, so that push is the whole release of the site.
* **Push to `main`** is gated by the ci-gate campaign
  (`scripts/ci.sh` = `check && test` + the coverage floor) and
  locally by the `pre-push` hook (`cargo xtask check`).

---
url: /myco/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

Install the `myco` CLI, then turn a repo's `project/` directory
into a work ledger — tasks, issues, proposals, plans, ADRs,
handoffs — that lives on its own orphan branch.

## Install

The crates.io name `myco` belongs to an unrelated project —
install from the repo. Pick one:

```sh
npm install -g 9aia/myco      # easiest — first `myco` run builds via cargo
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco myco
```

On npm ≥ 12, git fetches are gated — add `--allow-git=root`:
`npm install -g --allow-git=root 9aia/myco`.

The npm package is a thin shim — the first `myco` run builds the
Rust binary via `cargo install --git … myco` (there's no
postinstall; npm breaks lifecycle-script cwds on git installs),
so **Rust + cargo are still required** — the first build takes a
minute or two.

The trailing `myco` on the cargo command selects the package —
the repo is a workspace, so cargo needs to know which member to
install. To also get the
[pavo](https://github.com/9aia/pavo) view driver
(`tamias-driver-myco`, see below):

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco myco-driver
```

From a checkout of this repo: `cargo xtask install` builds and
installs the release binary to `~/.cargo/bin/myco`.

## Set up a repo

```sh
cd your-repo
myco init
```

`init` creates the orphan `project` branch, mounts it as a
`project/` worktree, seeds `meta.toml`, `TODO.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
`DONE.md`, `index.md` and the item dirs (`issues/`, `proposals/`, `plans/`,
`adrs/`, `handoffs/`), seeds a commented `[[kinds]]` prelude into
`myco.toml` at the repo root (only when absent), adds `project/`
to `.gitignore` on your
code branch, and writes a managed *Agent awareness* block into
`AGENTS.md`. It is idempotent — run it again and a healthy
worktree is verified, a damaged one repaired.

## First items

```sh
myco todo add "ship the thing" --pri high --label release
myco item set T-001 --status in-progress
myco status            # ledger digest
myco todo done T-001   # the line moves to DONE.md — still browsable
```

Every mutating verb is one atomic commit on the `project` branch —
the branch history is the audit trail. `--no-commit` (or the
`MYCO_NO_COMMIT` env var) opts out.

## The interactive board

`myco ui` opens a full-screen board over `TODO.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
and the file-backed kinds (issues, proposals, plans, ADRs) — the
human cockpit while agents drive the verbs. Every mutation runs
through the same ops the CLI uses, so a keypress that changes the
ledger lands as the same atomic commit (`--no-commit` opts out
here too). The board auto-reloads when the ledger changes on disk
— an OS filesystem watcher plus a content fingerprint catch other
`myco` invocations, `git pull`, and hand-edits — no keypress
needed; `R` forces one anyway.

| Key                            | Action                                       |
| ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab` / `Shift-Tab`, `1` / `2` / `3`, `h` / `l` | cycle / pick TODO / BACKLOG / FILES tabs |
| `j` / `k`, `gg` / `G`, `{`/`}` | move · ends · section jumps                  |
| `Enter`, `→`                  | item preview — `j`/`k` scroll, `←`/esc back   |
| `←`                           | back — pops the drill-down stack (esc-like in preview, no-op on the board) |
| `a`                            | add an item (TODO/BACKLOG only)              |
| `Space` / `dd`, `D`, `p`       | done · defer to BACKLOG · promote to TODO (done/undo ask `y`/`n`) |
| `u` / `U`                      | undo / redo ledger commits — `U` repeats while the redo stack lasts (asks `y`/`n`) |
| `Alt+j` / `Alt+k`              | reorder among siblings                       |
| `/`, `F`                       | live filter · clear it                       |
| `:`                            | command line — `:q` `:w` `:e` `:<id>` `:set` |
| `E`, `R`, `?`                  | `$EDITOR` · reload · keybind help            |
| `q`, `Ctrl-C`                  | quit                                         |
| click, wheel                   | select item / tab · scroll                   |
| double-click                   | open item preview                            |

`--view org-board` (or any `source = "index"` view) swaps the repo
ledger for the cross-repo index universe — rows are `repo:ID` and
verbs write the owning repo's worktree.

The TUI is a default cargo feature — for a lean binary without
it, install with `--no-default-features`:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco myco --no-default-features
```

## Visual views — pavo

For a read-only visual surface (and cross-repo org boards),
[pavo](https://github.com/9aia/pavo) renders the ledger through
`tamias-driver-myco` (the `myco-driver` crate in this repo):

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/myco myco-driver
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/pavo pavo   # the host, once
cd your-repo
pavo view myco:board     # TODO/BACKLOG tree — also myco:status,
                         # myco:items, myco:issues, …
pavo open myco:board     # same views in the pavo TUI
```

Run `pavo` inside the repo (or pass `--param
dir=…/project`) so the driver knows which ledger to open. The
driver's reads are view queries; writes ride the same engine
verbs — `tamias-driver-myco run <verb>` (or the driver's `ops`
manifest / `cli.<verb>` queries) reaches the full `myco` surface,
commit-per-mutation included. `myco ui` stays the interactive
path.

## Agent self-discovery

```sh
myco manifest          # capabilities + protocol version (JSON)
myco schema            # the file/state spec as JSON Schema
myco status --prompt   # token-sized digest for a context window
```

Every verb accepts `--json`. `myco check` validates the ledger —
file schemas, state machine, index drift — and `myco check --fix`
repairs what it safely can.

## Where next

* [Your first item](tutorials/first-item.md) — a guided walk
  through a full task lifecycle.
* [Set up myco on a repository](how-to/init-repo.md) — discovery,
  overrides, non-standard layouts.
* [The worktree model](explanation/worktree-model.md) — what is
  actually on disk and why.
* [CLI reference](reference/cli.md) — the full verb surface.
